# Step reference {#ch16}



## Recipe fields {#ref_recipe_fields}

[edition: Lite and Pro]

The recipe editor's **Details** tab shows these fields. **Tracks** is hidden there, because tracks are edited on the timeline: when a track is selected, its fields appear in the same tab and the **Recipe** category folds away.

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| >> Recipe |  |  |
| **Tracks** | empty (edited on the timeline) | Tracks of this recipe. Edited in the recipe timeline. |
| **Cooldown** | 0 s | Seconds before this recipe can play again on the same target. At least 0. |
| **Max Concurrent** | 0 | Maximum simultaneous instances per target. 0 means unlimited. At least 0. |
| **Default Intensity** | 1 | Multiplier applied to every play of this recipe. At least 0. |
| **Schema Version** | 0 | Version of the recipe data format, written on save. 0 for recipes saved before versioning. Read only. Under the advanced arrow of its category. |
| >> Parameters |  |  |
| **Parameters** | empty | **Pro.** Named numbers the game can pass each time the recipe plays. Tracks can scale their intensity by them through parameter mappings, and the recipe editor shows a slider for each to preview the range. A parameter named Distance is filled in automatically when the game does not pass it. |
| >> Sustain |  |  |
| **Sustain** | Off | **Pro.** Keeps the recipe playing while a condition lasts: time loops between Sustain Start and Sustain End until the play is released (Release Feel, the end of an anim notify state, or Stop Feel), then plays the rest of the recipe. |
| **Sustain Start** | 0 s | **Pro.** Start of the looping region, in seconds from the recipe start. At least 0. Editable only when **Sustain** is on. |
| **Sustain End** | 1 s | **Pro.** End of the looping region, in seconds from the recipe start. At least 0. Editable only when **Sustain** is on. |
| >> Library |  |  |
| **Feeling** | None | **Pro.** What this recipe makes the player feel. It groups the recipe browser and the recipe library, for example Feel.Feeling.Impact. Projects can add their own tags under Feel.Feeling. Editor only: not included in packaged games. |
| **Genres** | empty | **Pro.** Kinds of game this recipe suits, for example Feel.Genre.Shooter. Used by the recipe browser filters. Editor only: not included in packaged games. |
| **Description** | empty | **Pro.** One or two sentences describing the recipe, shown in the recipe browser and the Content Browser tooltip. Editor only: not included in packaged games. |
| **Based On** | None | **Pro.** The library recipe this one was copied from, when it was created with Recipe from Template. Read only. Editor only: not included in packaged games. |
| >> Preview |  |  |
| **Preview Mesh** | None | Mesh shown in the recipe editor preview. Static or skeletal; empty shows a cube. Editor only: not included in packaged games. |

Each entry of **Parameters**:
{widths: 26,20,54}
| Field | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Name** | None | Name the game uses to pass a value, and tracks use to read it. A parameter named Distance is special: when the game does not pass it, it is filled in with the distance in centimeters from the play's target to the nearest local player camera. |
| **Default Value** | 0 | Value used when the game does not pass one. |
| **Min Value** | 0 | Lowest meaningful value. Lower values are clamped to it. Track mappings read this as 0. |
| **Max Value** | 1 | Highest meaningful value. Higher values are clamped to it. Track mappings read this as 1. |
| **Accumulator** | None | Optional accumulator (Project Settings > Plugins > FeelKit > Accumulators) this parameter reads when the game does not pass a value. It is read every frame while the recipe plays: the value stored for the play's target actor, else the value of the play's instigator, else the global value. Leave empty to use the default value. |
| **Description** | empty | Explains what the value represents, for whoever sets it. Shown as the tooltip of the preview slider. |

## Track fields {#ref_track_fields}

[edition: Lite and Pro]

Select a track on the timeline to see these fields in **Details**. The fields of the **Track** category appear under the track's number (**Track 1**, **Track 2** and so on), followed by **Parameter Mappings**, **Randomness**, **Comfort** and **Conditions**. The settings of the track's step are inside **Step**.

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| >> Track |  |  |
| **Step** | None (chosen with **+ Track**) | The effect this track plays. |
| **Start Time** | 0 s | Seconds from recipe start. At least 0. |
| **Duration** | 0.5 s | Length in seconds. 0 means an instant step. At least 0. |
| **Channel** | the step's default channel | Channel of this track, for example Feel.Camera.Shake. |
| **Intensity Curve** | fades from 1 to 0 | Intensity over the track's normalized time, from 0 at its start to 1 at its end. An empty curve means a constant 1. New tracks of steps that shape their own motion start with a flat curve at 1. |
| **Seed** | 0 | Seed for noise and randomness in the step. |
| **Applies To** | Play Target | **Pro.** Which actor this track's actor effects (scale, materials, actor time, attached sounds, Blueprint events) apply to: the play's target, or the Instigator actor passed in the play context. Camera, screen and haptic effects go to the local player of that actor. |
| **Enabled** | On | Editor mute. Disabled tracks produce no output, in the preview and in the game. |
| >> Parameter Mappings |  |  |
| **Parameter Mappings** | empty | **Pro.** Recipe parameters that scale this track's intensity. Each mapping multiplies the intensity; they combine with the intensity curve. |
| >> Randomness |  |  |
| **Random Intensity** | Min 1, Max 1 | **Pro.** Intensity multiplier picked at random between Min and Max for each play. 1 to 1 means no variation. |
| **Random Duration Scale** | Min 1, Max 1 | **Pro.** Length multiplier picked at random between Min and Max for each play. 1 to 1 means no variation. |
| >> Comfort |  |  |
| **Essential** | Off | Marks the track as carrying gameplay-critical information. |
| **Substitute Step** | None | Played instead when comfort settings disable this channel and the track is essential. |
| **Essential Floor** | 0 | Minimum intensity scale when the track is essential and has no substitute. Range 0 to 1. |
| >> Conditions |  |  |
| **Local Player Only** | Off | **Pro.** Only play when the target belongs to a local player. |
| **Max Distance** | 0 cm | **Pro.** Skip when the target is farther than this from the local camera. 0 means unlimited. At least 0. |
| **Chance** | 1 | **Pro.** Probability that the track plays. Range 0 to 1. |
| **Platforms** | empty | **Pro.** Platforms the track plays on. Empty means all platforms. |

Each entry of **Parameter Mappings**:
{widths: 26,20,54}
| Field | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Parameter** | None | Recipe parameter this mapping reads. |
| **Curve** | straight line from 0 to 1 | How the parameter turns into an intensity multiplier. Horizontal axis: the parameter from its min (0) to its max (1). Vertical axis: the multiplier applied to the track. The default straight line from 0 to 1 means intensity grows in proportion to the parameter. An empty curve behaves like that line. |

## Reading the step entries {#ref_step_entries}

Every step below has the same parts:

- **Class** and module: the C++ class, for searching the source and for C++ code. The **+ Track** menu of the recipe editor lists steps by their display name, which is the heading of the entry.
- **Default channel**: the channel a new track of this step gets. You can change it on the track; comfort and arbitration follow the track's channel, not the step.
- **Comfort group**: the group that scales the default channel under the default **Channel Comfort Groups** in the project settings ([see: set_comfort]).
- **Editor preview**: whether the recipe editor's preview shows the step. Steps it cannot show still play in the game, and their tracks carry a **No preview** label.
- **Track length**: steps that act once when the track starts can sit on an instant track of length 0.
- **New tracks start with**: the intensity curve a new track of the step gets.
- The table: every setting of the step as the **Details** tab shows it, with its default and units, followed by what it does, its allowed range and when the editor shows it.
- **Checks when the recipe is saved**: problems with the step's settings that data validation reports.

Rotation values are listed as pitch, yaw and roll. The **Details** tab shows a rotator as X (roll), Y (pitch) and Z (yaw). Camera offsets are in camera space: X points forward, Y right and Z up.

## Shared motion settings {#ref_motion_settings}

[edition: Lite and Pro]

Camera Punch, FOV Kick and the other steps in the table below move along a motion shape. The shape gives the form of the motion over the track, from 0 to a peak of 1 and back; the step's own settings give the size at the peak, and the track's intensity multiplies the result. New tracks of these steps start with a flat intensity curve, so the shape alone sets the motion.

With **Spring**, the motion follows time in seconds, not the length of the track: a track shorter than the spring's settling time cuts the motion off, and a longer track stays at rest after it settles. **Kick** and **Smooth** stretch to fill the track. **Repeats** splits the track into equal parts and plays the shape once in each.

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Shape** | Spring | How the motion moves over the track. |
| **Frequency** | 5 Hz | Spring oscillations per second. At least 0.1. Shown only when **Shape** is **Spring**. |
| **Damping** | 7 | How quickly the spring settles. Higher values bounce less. At least 0. Shown only when **Shape** is **Spring**. |
| **Attack Fraction** | 0.15 | Portion of the track spent rising to the peak. Range 0.01 to 0.99. Shown only when **Shape** is **Kick**. |
| **Repeats** | 1 | Plays the shape this many times across the track, for heartbeats, double hits and flurries. Range 1 to 32. |

Shapes:

- **Spring**: Springy overshoot that settles, like a physical hit.
- **Kick**: Fast rise to the peak, then an eased return.
- **Smooth**: Smooth rise and fall.

Default shape of each step that uses these settings:

{widths: 50,50}
| Step | Default shape |
|---|---|
| [name: step_camera_punch] | Spring |
| [name: step_fov_kick] | Kick |
| [name: step_camera_roll] | Spring |
| [name: step_look_at_nudge] | Kick |
| [name: step_vignette_pulse] | Smooth |
| [name: step_chromatic_aberration] | Kick |
| [name: step_desaturate] | Smooth |
| [name: step_color_tint] | Smooth |
| [name: step_post_process_material_pulse] | Smooth |
| [name: step_squash_and_stretch] | Spring |
| [name: step_material_parameter_pulse] | Smooth |
| [name: step_hit_flash] | Smooth |
| [name: step_light_flash] | Kick |
| [name: step_force_feedback_curve] | Kick |
| [name: step_widget_punch] | Spring |
| [name: step_widget_flash] | Kick |

## Camera steps {#ref_steps_camera}

Camera steps offset the view of the target's local player, through a camera modifier that FeelKit adds to each local player's camera manager. Tracks of one play add up; separate plays are combined by the **Camera Arbitration** setting ([see: set_camera]).

### Procedural Shake {#step_procedural_shake}

[edition: Lite and Pro]

Moves and turns the camera with noise or a sine wave computed from the track time and the seed, so the same seed gives the same shake every time and the preview shows exact frames when scrubbing. **Perlin** gives smooth random motion on each axis. **Sine** gives a regular oscillation with a random phase per axis. **Directional** moves back and forth along **Direction** only, with the rotation swinging in step. The intensity curve sets the strength over time; the default curve gives a shake that dies away over the track.

- **Class:** `UFeelStep_ProceduralShake`, module FeelCore.
- **Default channel:** `Feel.Camera.Shake`.
- **Comfort group:** Camera Shake.
- **Editor preview:** yes.
- **Track length:** needs a length.
- **New tracks start with:** an intensity curve that fades from 1 to 0.

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Mode** | Perlin | Shape of the shake. |
| **Frequency** | 12 Hz | Oscillations per second. At least 0.01. |
| **Location Amplitude** | (0, 3, 3) cm | Maximum location offset per camera axis (X forward, Y right, Z up). Shown only when **Mode** is not **Directional**. |
| **Direction** | (0, 0, 1) | Camera-space direction of a directional shake. Shown only when **Mode** is **Directional**. |
| **Directional Amplitude** | 8 cm | Maximum offset along Direction. Shown only when **Mode** is **Directional**. |
| **Rotation Amplitude** | Pitch 1, Yaw 1, Roll 0.5 (degrees) | Maximum rotation offset in degrees per axis. |
| **Field Of View Amplitude** | 0° | Maximum field of view change. |

### Camera Punch {#step_camera_punch}

[edition: Lite and Pro]

Pushes and turns the camera to a peak and back along the motion shape; with the default Spring it overshoots and settles like a physical hit. **Location Punch** and **Rotation Punch** are the offsets at the peak. **Direction Source** can point the punch along the play's Direction, or away from or toward the play's Location, as seen from the camera when the play started. The strength stays that of the step settings, and the step settings are used when the play passed no direction or location. **Direction Jitter** turns the direction by a random angle for each play, which stays fixed for the whole play.

- **Class:** `UFeelStep_CameraPunch`, module FeelCore.
- **Default channel:** `Feel.Camera.Motion`.
- **Comfort group:** Camera Motion.
- **Editor preview:** yes.
- **Track length:** needs a length.
- **New tracks start with:** a flat intensity curve at 1.
- **Motion shape:** Spring by default; the shape settings are described in [ref: ref_motion_settings].

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Location Punch** | (-10, 0, -4) cm | Camera-space location offset at the peak (X forward, Y right, Z up). |
| **Rotation Punch** | Pitch -2.5, Yaw 0, Roll 0 (degrees) | Rotation offset at the peak, in degrees. |
| **Direction Source** | Step Settings | Where the punch direction comes from. With a play direction or location, the punch keeps the strength of Location Punch and Rotation Punch but points along that direction, as seen from the camera when the play started. |
| **Direction Jitter** | 0° | Varies the punch direction per play by up to this angle, so repeated plays never look identical. Range 0 to 90. |

### FOV Kick {#step_fov_kick}

[edition: Lite and Pro]

Changes the field of view by **Field Of View Kick** at the peak and back. Positive values widen the view, which reads as speed; negative values narrow it, which reads as an impact zoom. The default Kick shape rises fast and eases back.

- **Class:** `UFeelStep_FOVKick`, module FeelCore.
- **Default channel:** `Feel.Camera.Motion`.
- **Comfort group:** Camera Motion.
- **Editor preview:** yes.
- **Track length:** needs a length.
- **New tracks start with:** a flat intensity curve at 1.
- **Motion shape:** Kick by default; the shape settings are described in [ref: ref_motion_settings].

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Field Of View Kick** | 8° | Field of view change at the peak. Positive widens (speed), negative narrows (impact zoom). Range -60 to 60. |

### Camera Roll {#step_camera_roll}

[edition: Pro]

Rolls the camera around its view axis to **Roll Degrees** at the peak and back. With **Random Direction** on, each play picks clockwise or counterclockwise from its seed. Players who turn **Allow Camera Roll** off in their comfort settings see no camera roll from any recipe.

- **Class:** `UFeelStep_CameraRoll`, module FeelCore.
- **Default channel:** `Feel.Camera.Motion`.
- **Comfort group:** Camera Motion; the roll is also removed completely when a player turns **Allow Camera Roll** off.
- **Editor preview:** yes.
- **Track length:** needs a length.
- **New tracks start with:** a flat intensity curve at 1.
- **Motion shape:** Spring by default; the shape settings are described in [ref: ref_motion_settings].

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Roll Degrees** | 4° | Roll angle at the peak. Positive rolls clockwise. Range -45 to 45. |
| **Random Direction** | On | Pick clockwise or counterclockwise at random for each play. |

### Camera Zoom {#step_camera_zoom}

[edition: Pro]

Eases the field of view by **Field Of View Change** over the first part of the track (**Ease in Fraction**), holds it, and eases back over the last part (**Ease Out Fraction**). Negative values zoom in. The track length sets how long the zoom holds.

- **Class:** `UFeelStep_CameraZoom`, module FeelCore.
- **Default channel:** `Feel.Camera.Motion`.
- **Comfort group:** Camera Motion.
- **Editor preview:** yes.
- **Track length:** needs a length.
- **New tracks start with:** a flat intensity curve at 1.

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Field Of View Change** | -10° | Field of view change while held. Negative zooms in, positive zooms out. Range -60 to 60. |
| **Ease in Fraction** | 0.25 | Portion of the track spent easing into the zoom. Range 0 to 1. |
| **Ease Out Fraction** | 0.35 | Portion of the track spent easing back out. Range 0 to 1. |

### Look-at Nudge {#step_look_at_nudge}

[edition: Pro]

Turns the camera part of the way toward the play's Location, or along the play's Direction when it passed no location, and back. **Turn Fraction** is the share of the angle to that point reached at the peak, and **Max Turn Degrees** limits the turn in yaw and in pitch. A play with neither a location nor a direction produces no motion.

- **Class:** `UFeelStep_LookAtNudge`, module FeelCore.
- **Default channel:** `Feel.Camera.Motion`.
- **Comfort group:** Camera Motion.
- **Editor preview:** yes.
- **Track length:** needs a length.
- **New tracks start with:** a flat intensity curve at 1.
- **Motion shape:** Kick by default; the shape settings are described in [ref: ref_motion_settings].

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Turn Fraction** | 0.2 | Portion of the angle to the location that the camera turns at the peak. Range 0 to 1. |
| **Max Turn Degrees** | 6° | Largest turn at the peak, per axis. Range 0 to 45. |

## Time steps {#ref_steps_time}

Time steps change time dilation. Recipes are timed in real time, so a track keeps its length and the rest of the recipe keeps playing while the world is slowed. When time requests overlap on the same clock, the highest **Priority** wins, and among equal priorities the slowest dilation wins. When no request remains, the clock gets back the dilation it had before FeelKit changed it. In networked games a global request slows only the play's target unless **Allow Global Time Dilation in Multiplayer** is on ([see: set_playback]).

### Global Hitstop {#step_global_hitstop}

[edition: Lite and Pro]

Slows the whole world to **Time Dilation** while the track plays. The track's intensity, clamped to 0 to 1, blends between normal speed at 0 and **Time Dilation** at 1, so a flat curve gives a hard stop and a fading curve lets time recover over the track. The editor preview cannot slow time; use **Play in PIE** to judge a hitstop.

- **Class:** `UFeelStep_GlobalHitstop`, module FeelCore.
- **Default channel:** `Feel.Time.Hitstop`.
- **Comfort group:** Hitstop and Slow-mo.
- **Editor preview:** no, the track shows **No preview**.
- **Track length:** needs a length.
- **New tracks start with:** a flat intensity curve at 1.

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Time Dilation** | 0.05 | Time dilation at full intensity. Small values freeze the action. Range 0.0001 to 1. |
| **Priority** | 0 | When hitstops on the same clock overlap, the highest priority wins. |

### Actor Hitstop {#step_actor_hitstop}

[edition: Pro]

Works like Global Hitstop, but slows only one actor through its custom time dilation, so the rest of the world keeps moving: the play's target, or the instigator when the track's **Applies To** is Instigator.

- **Class:** `UFeelStep_ActorHitstop`, module FeelCore.
- **Default channel:** `Feel.Time.Hitstop`.
- **Comfort group:** Hitstop and Slow-mo.
- **Editor preview:** no, the track shows **No preview**.
- **Track length:** needs a length.
- **New tracks start with:** a flat intensity curve at 1.

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Time Dilation** | 0.05 | Time dilation at full intensity. Small values freeze the action. Range 0.0001 to 1. |
| **Priority** | 0 | When hitstops on the same clock overlap, the highest priority wins. |

### Slow-mo Ramp {#step_slow_mo_ramp}

[edition: Lite and Pro]

Eases the whole world into slow motion over **Ramp in Time**, holds at **Time Dilation**, and eases back to normal speed over **Ramp Out Time** before the track ends. Both ramps are real seconds with a smooth start and end. The intensity, clamped to 0 to 1, sets how far time slows: at 0.5 it slows half as far.

- **Class:** `UFeelStep_SlowMoRamp`, module FeelCore.
- **Default channel:** `Feel.Time.SlowMo`.
- **Comfort group:** Hitstop and Slow-mo.
- **Editor preview:** no, the track shows **No preview**.
- **Track length:** needs a length.
- **New tracks start with:** a flat intensity curve at 1.

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Time Dilation** | 0.3 | Time dilation while fully slowed. Range 0.0001 to 1. |
| **Ramp in Time** | 0.15 s | Real seconds to ease into slow motion at the start of the track. At least 0. |
| **Ramp Out Time** | 0.3 s | Real seconds to ease back to normal speed before the track ends. At least 0. |
| **Priority** | 0 | When slow motions and hitstops overlap, the highest priority wins; equal priorities keep the slowest. |

## Screen steps {#ref_steps_screen}

Screen steps change the whole view of the target's local player. Flashes and fades are drawn over the view; tints, vignette, chromatic aberration, saturation and post-process materials are blended into the view's post-process settings. Across separate plays the strongest contribution wins for each of these.

### Screen Flash {#step_screen_flash}

[edition: Lite and Pro]

Covers the view with **Color** at up to **Max Opacity**, drawn on top of the game's own camera fades. The intensity curve shapes the flash: the default curve starts at full opacity and clears over the track. Screen Flash tracks count toward the flash limiter of each player's comfort settings.

- **Class:** `UFeelStep_ScreenFlash`, module FeelCore.
- **Default channel:** `Feel.Screen.Flash`.
- **Comfort group:** Flashes.
- **Editor preview:** yes.
- **Track length:** needs a length.
- **New tracks start with:** an intensity curve that fades from 1 to 0.

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Color** | White (R 1, G 1, B 1) | Flash color. |
| **Max Opacity** | 0.6 | Opacity at full intensity. Range 0 to 1. |

### Vignette Pulse {#step_vignette_pulse}

[edition: Lite and Pro]

Darkens the edges of the view by blending the scene's vignette toward **Vignette Intensity** and back. The engine's own vignette is about 0.4, so values near 1 give a strong darkening. With **Repeats** above 1 it pulses several times across the track, for example as a heartbeat.

- **Class:** `UFeelStep_VignettePulse`, module FeelCore.
- **Default channel:** `Feel.Screen.Distortion`.
- **Comfort group:** Screen Distortion.
- **Editor preview:** yes.
- **Track length:** needs a length.
- **New tracks start with:** a flat intensity curve at 1.
- **Motion shape:** Smooth by default; the shape settings are described in [ref: ref_motion_settings].

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Vignette Intensity** | 1 | Vignette intensity at the peak, blended over the scene's own vignette (the engine default is about 0.4). Range 0 to 1. |

### Chromatic Aberration {#step_chromatic_aberration}

[edition: Pro]

Splits the colors toward the edges of the view by blending the scene's chromatic aberration toward **Fringe Intensity** and back. The default Kick shape rises fast and eases back.

- **Class:** `UFeelStep_ChromaticAberration`, module FeelCore.
- **Default channel:** `Feel.Screen.Distortion`.
- **Comfort group:** Screen Distortion.
- **Editor preview:** yes.
- **Track length:** needs a length.
- **New tracks start with:** a flat intensity curve at 1.
- **Motion shape:** Kick by default; the shape settings are described in [ref: ref_motion_settings].

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Fringe Intensity** | 3 | Chromatic aberration intensity at the peak, blended over the scene's own setting. Range 0 to 5. |

### Desaturate {#step_desaturate}

[edition: Pro]

Drains color from the scene and brings it back. **Amount** 1 makes the picture grayscale at the peak; the default 0.8 leaves a trace of color.

- **Class:** `UFeelStep_Desaturate`, module FeelCore.
- **Default channel:** `Feel.Screen.Color`.
- **Comfort group:** Screen Distortion.
- **Editor preview:** yes.
- **Track length:** needs a length.
- **New tracks start with:** a flat intensity curve at 1.
- **Motion shape:** Smooth by default; the shape settings are described in [ref: ref_motion_settings].

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Amount** | 0.8 | How much color is removed at the peak: 1 is grayscale. Range 0 to 1. |

### Color Tint {#step_color_tint}

[edition: Pro]

Multiplies the scene toward **Tint Color** and back. **Strength** sets how far the scene moves toward the tint at the peak. A white tint leaves the scene unchanged.

- **Class:** `UFeelStep_ColorTint`, module FeelCore.
- **Default channel:** `Feel.Screen.Color`.
- **Comfort group:** Screen Distortion.
- **Editor preview:** yes.
- **Track length:** needs a length.
- **New tracks start with:** a flat intensity curve at 1.
- **Motion shape:** Smooth by default; the shape settings are described in [ref: ref_motion_settings].

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Tint Color** | R 1, G 0.4, B 0.35 | Color the scene is multiplied toward. White leaves it unchanged. |
| **Strength** | 1 | How far the scene moves toward the tint at the peak. Range 0 to 1. |

### Screen Fade {#step_screen_fade}

[edition: Pro]

Fades the view to **Fade Color**, holds, and fades back: the first **Fade In Fraction** of the track fades in, the last **Fade Out Fraction** fades out, and the view holds at **Max Opacity** in between. With **Fade Out Fraction** at 0 the view stays faded until the track ends. The fade is drawn under flashes, so a flash during a fade stays visible.

- **Class:** `UFeelStep_ScreenFade`, module FeelCore.
- **Default channel:** `Feel.Screen.Fade`.
- **Comfort group:** none, only Master applies.
- **Editor preview:** yes.
- **Track length:** needs a length.
- **New tracks start with:** a flat intensity curve at 1.

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Fade Color** | Black (R 0, G 0, B 0) | Color faded to. |
| **Max Opacity** | 1 | Opacity while held. Range 0 to 1. |
| **Fade in Fraction** | 0.3 | Portion of the track spent fading in. Range 0 to 1. |
| **Fade Out Fraction** | 0.3 | Portion of the track spent fading out. 0 stays faded until the track ends. Range 0 to 1. |

### Post Process Material Pulse {#step_post_process_material_pulse}

[edition: Pro]

Blends a post-process material over the scene and back, for effects the engine has no setting for, such as radial blur, scanlines or heat haze. The material must use the Post Process material domain. Unreal draws an active post-process material at full strength, so FeelKit passes the current weight, from 0 to 1, to the scalar parameter named in **Weight Parameter**. The material should use that value to fade its own effect, for example as the Alpha of a Lerp from Scene Texture PostProcessInput0 to the effect. The sample material `M_FK_PP_Pulse` in /FeelKit/Samples/Materials is set up this way.

- **Class:** `UFeelStep_PostProcessMaterialPulse`, module FeelCore.
- **Default channel:** `Feel.Screen.Distortion`.
- **Comfort group:** Screen Distortion.
- **Editor preview:** yes.
- **Track length:** needs a length.
- **New tracks start with:** a flat intensity curve at 1.
- **Motion shape:** Smooth by default; the shape settings are described in [ref: ref_motion_settings].

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Material** | None | Post-process material to blend in. |
| **Max Weight** | 1 | Blend weight at the peak. Range 0 to 1. |
| **Weight Parameter** | `Weight` | Scalar parameter of the material that receives the current weight (0 to 1), so the material can fade its own effect, for example as the Alpha of a Lerp from the scene (Scene Texture: PostProcessInput0) to the effect. Unreal shows a post-process material at full strength whenever it is active, so a material without this parameter appears at full strength for the whole track. Set to None to blend the material directly. |

Checks when the recipe is saved:

- Error: "Post Process Material Pulse has no material."

## Actor steps {#ref_steps_actor}

Actor steps change the actor the track applies to: the play's target, or the instigator when the track's **Applies To** is Instigator. On an actor whose root takes part in collision, such as a character's capsule, motion and scale go to its visible child components, so collision and movement stay unchanged. FeelKit restores every original value once no track changes it any more.

### Scale Punch {#step_scale_punch}

[edition: Lite and Pro]

Scales the target up by **Amount** and back with a springy swing: the scale starts and ends at the target's own scale, and each of the **Bounces** adds one more swing below and above it in between. **Amount** is relative, so 0.3 makes the target 30% larger at the peak. The intensity curve sets how quickly the swings die down.

- **Class:** `UFeelStep_ScalePunch`, module FeelCore.
- **Default channel:** `Feel.Actor.Transform`.
- **Comfort group:** none, only Master applies.
- **Editor preview:** yes.
- **Track length:** needs a length.
- **New tracks start with:** an intensity curve that fades from 1 to 0.

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Amount** | (0.3, 0.3, 0.3) | Relative scale change at the peak, per axis. 0.3 means 30% larger. |
| **Bounces** | 1 | Extra bounces after the first swing. Range 0 to 10. |

### Squash and Stretch {#step_squash_and_stretch}

[edition: Lite and Pro]

Stretches the target along its local **Axis** by **Amount** at the peak; negative amounts squash it. With **Preserve Volume** on, the other two axes thin out while it stretches and bulge while it squashes, so the target keeps its volume. With the default Spring shape a stretch overshoots into a squash before it settles.

- **Class:** `UFeelStep_SquashStretch`, module FeelCore.
- **Default channel:** `Feel.Actor.Transform`.
- **Comfort group:** none, only Master applies.
- **Editor preview:** yes.
- **Track length:** needs a length.
- **New tracks start with:** a flat intensity curve at 1.
- **Motion shape:** Spring by default; the shape settings are described in [ref: ref_motion_settings].

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Axis** | Z | Local axis the target stretches along. |
| **Amount** | 0.3 | Stretch at the peak. 0.3 makes the target 30% longer along the axis; negative values squash. A spring overshoots into the opposite. Range -0.9 to 3. |
| **Preserve Volume** | On | Keeps volume constant: the other axes thin out while stretching and bulge while squashing. |

### Material Parameter Pulse {#step_material_parameter_pulse}

[edition: Pro]

Pulses material parameters on the target's meshes and puts their original values back afterwards. For each entry of **Parameters**, a color parameter blends from its original color toward **Color**, or a scalar parameter gets **Scalar Amount** added at the peak. **Route** chooses how the values reach the materials: **Material Instance** creates dynamic material instances and works with any material parameter; **Custom Primitive Data** needs no material instances, but the material has to read the parameter as custom primitive data. When several tracks pulse the same parameter, scalar changes add up and the strongest color wins.

- **Class:** `UFeelStep_MaterialPulse`, module FeelCore.
- **Default channel:** `Feel.Actor.Material`.
- **Comfort group:** none, only Master applies.
- **Editor preview:** yes.
- **Track length:** needs a length.
- **New tracks start with:** a flat intensity curve at 1.
- **Motion shape:** Smooth by default; the shape settings are described in [ref: ref_motion_settings].

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Parameters** | one entry with the defaults below | Parameters pulsed together. |
| **Route** | Material Instance | How the parameters reach the materials. |

Each entry of **Parameters**:

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Field | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Parameter Name** | `Color` | Name of the material parameter. |
| **Is Color** | On | Blend a color parameter toward Color instead of offsetting a scalar parameter. |
| **Scalar Amount** | 1 | Added to the scalar parameter's original value at the peak. Shown only when **Is Color** is off. |
| **Color** | R 1, G 0.15, B 0.1 | Color reached at the peak, blended from the parameter's original color. Shown only when **Is Color** is on. |

Checks when the recipe is saved:

- Warning: "Material Parameter Pulse has no parameters, so it does nothing."
- Error: "Material Parameter Pulse has a parameter without a name."

### Hit Flash {#step_hit_flash}

[edition: Pro]

Flashes the target's meshes with **Color** by drawing an instance of **Flash Material** in each mesh's overlay material slot, so it works on any mesh without changes to its own materials. The flash material must be a translucent overlay material with a vector parameter FlashColor and a scalar parameter FlashAmount from 0 to 1. The sample `M_FK_HitFlash` in /FeelKit/Samples/Materials is one. The mesh's own overlay material is put back afterwards.

- **Class:** `UFeelStep_HitFlash`, module FeelCore.
- **Default channel:** `Feel.Actor.Material`.
- **Comfort group:** none, only Master applies.
- **Editor preview:** yes.
- **Track length:** needs a length.
- **New tracks start with:** a flat intensity curve at 1.
- **Motion shape:** Smooth by default; the shape settings are described in [ref: ref_motion_settings].

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Flash Material** | None | Overlay material drawn over the meshes. It reads FlashColor (vector) and FlashAmount (scalar, 0 to 1). |
| **Color** | White (R 1, G 1, B 1) | Flash color at the peak. |

Checks when the recipe is saved:

- Warning: "Hit Flash has no flash material, so it does nothing. Pick a translucent overlay material with FlashColor and FlashAmount parameters."

### Mesh Wobble {#step_mesh_wobble}

[edition: Pro]

Tilts and moves the target back and forth around wherever it is, fading out over the track, so it also works on moving targets. **Tilt Amplitude** and **Move Amplitude** are the largest swings at the start, **Frequency** the swings per second, and **Decay** how quickly the swing dies: 0 keeps full strength, 1 fades linearly and higher values fade faster. Each axis swings with its own phase. **Noise** replaces the regular swing with irregular motion. A component whose physics simulates, such as a ragdoll, is left to physics.

- **Class:** `UFeelStep_MeshWobble`, module FeelCore.
- **Default channel:** `Feel.Actor.Transform`.
- **Comfort group:** none, only Master applies.
- **Editor preview:** yes.
- **Track length:** needs a length.
- **New tracks start with:** a flat intensity curve at 1.

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Tilt Amplitude** | Pitch 0, Yaw 0, Roll 8 (degrees) | Largest tilt around each local axis at the start, in degrees. |
| **Move Amplitude** | (0, 0, 0) cm | Largest movement along each local axis at the start, in centimeters. |
| **Frequency** | 10 Hz | Wobbles per second. Range 0.1 to 60. |
| **Decay** | 1.5 | How quickly the wobble dies down over the track. 0 keeps full strength to the end; 1 fades linearly; higher fades faster. Range 0 to 8. |
| **Noise** | Off | Irregular noise motion instead of a regular back-and-forth swing. |

### Light Flash {#step_light_flash}

[edition: Pro]

Brightens the target's lights and can shift their color, then returns them. **Intensity Change** is a multiple of each light's own intensity: 2 makes it three times as bright and -1 turns it off. It applies to the target when the target is a light component, and otherwise to every light component of the target actor. **Color Strength** moves the light color toward **Color**. With **Flicker** on, the light switches between flashed and normal **Flicker Rate** times per second, in an on and off pattern taken from the seed. Light Flash tracks count toward the flash limiter under the default channel mapping.

- **Class:** `UFeelStep_LightFlash`, module FeelCore.
- **Default channel:** `Feel.Actor.Light`.
- **Comfort group:** Flashes.
- **Editor preview:** no, the track shows **No preview**.
- **Track length:** needs a length.
- **New tracks start with:** a flat intensity curve at 1.
- **Motion shape:** Kick by default; the shape settings are described in [ref: ref_motion_settings].

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| >> Light |  |  |
| **Intensity Change** | 2 | Extra brightness at the peak, as a multiple of the light's own intensity: 2 makes it three times as bright, -1 turns it off. Applies to the target when it is a light component, otherwise to every light component of the target actor. Range -1 to 50. |
| **Color** | White (R 1, G 1, B 1) | Color the light moves toward. |
| **Color Strength** | 0 | How far the light color moves toward Color at the peak. 0 keeps the light's color. Range 0 to 1. |
| >> Flicker |  |  |
| **Flicker** | Off | Rapidly switch between bright and normal while the track plays, like an unstable light. |
| **Flicker Rate** | 18 Hz | Flicker changes per second. Range 1 to 60. Editable only when **Flicker** is on. |

## Audio steps {#ref_steps_audio}

Audio steps play sounds or change the mix. They have no comfort group under the default mapping, so only Master scales them.

### Play Sound {#step_play_sound}

[edition: Lite and Pro]

Plays **Sound** when the track starts, in 2D, attached to the target (at **Attach Socket Name** when set) or at the target's location. **Attached to Target** falls back to the target's location when the target has no component. Each play varies the volume and pitch at random by up to **Volume Variation** and **Pitch Variation**. With **Scale Volume with Intensity** on, the volume follows the track's intensity at the moment the track starts, comfort included. On a track with a length, **Stop at Track End** and **Stop when Recipe Stops** fade the sound out over **Fade Out Time**; on an instant track the sound simply plays to its end. The sound is audible in the editor preview.

- **Class:** `UFeelStep_PlaySound`, module FeelCore.
- **Default channel:** `Feel.Audio`.
- **Comfort group:** none, only Master applies.
- **Editor preview:** yes, the sound is audible.
- **Track length:** can be an instant track (length 0).
- **New tracks start with:** an intensity curve that fades from 1 to 0.

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| >> Sound |  |  |
| **Sound** | None | Sound to play. |
| **Placement** | 2D | Where the sound plays. |
| **Attach Socket Name** | None | Socket or bone to attach to. Leave empty for the component origin. Shown only when **Placement** is **Attached to Target**. |
| **Volume Multiplier** | 1 | Volume at full intensity. Range 0 to 4. |
| **Scale Volume with Intensity** | On | Scale the volume with the track's intensity, including comfort settings. |
| **Pitch Multiplier** | 1 | Pitch multiplier. Range 0.1 to 4. |
| **Sound Start Time** | 0 s | Seconds into the sound to start playing. At least 0. |
| **Attenuation Settings** | None | Attenuation for positioned sounds. Leave empty to use the sound's own. Shown only when **Placement** is not **2D**. |
| **Concurrency Settings** | None | Concurrency settings. Leave empty to use the sound's own. |
| >> Variation |  |  |
| **Volume Variation** | 0.05 | Random volume change per play, as a fraction: 0.1 varies the volume by up to 10%. Range 0 to 1. |
| **Pitch Variation** | 0.05 | Random pitch change per play, as a fraction. A little variation keeps repeated sounds from feeling mechanical. Range 0 to 0.5. |
| >> Stopping |  |  |
| **Stop at Track End** | Off | Fade the sound out when the track ends. Only for tracks with a length. |
| **Stop when Recipe Stops** | On | Fade the sound out when the recipe is stopped early. Only for tracks with a length. |
| **Fade Out Time** | 0.15 s | Fade-out length when the sound is stopped. At least 0. |

Checks when the recipe is saved:

- Error: "Play Sound has no sound."

### Sound Class Duck {#step_sound_class_duck}

[edition: Pro]

Lowers the volume of **Sound Class** and its child classes, then brings it back. The change builds up over the first **Attack Fraction** of the track, holds, and releases over the last **Release Fraction**. **Volume Reduction** 1 silences the class at full intensity. With **Sound Class** empty, the project's default sound class is used (Project Settings > Audio). FeelKit applies the change through a sound mix it creates while the track plays. When several tracks change the same class, the lowest volume wins.

- **Class:** `UFeelStep_SoundClassDuck`, module FeelCore.
- **Default channel:** `Feel.Audio.Mix`.
- **Comfort group:** none, only Master applies.
- **Editor preview:** yes.
- **Track length:** needs a length.
- **New tracks start with:** a flat intensity curve at 1.

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Sound Class** | None | Sound class to adjust, including its child classes. Leave empty for the project's default sound class (Project Settings > Audio). |
| **Attack Fraction** | 0.1 | Portion of the track spent moving to the full adjustment. Range 0 to 1. |
| **Release Fraction** | 0.4 | Portion of the track spent returning to normal. Range 0 to 1. |
| **Volume Reduction** | 0.6 | Portion of the volume removed at full strength: 1 silences the class. Range 0 to 1. |

### Pitch Bend {#step_pitch_bend}

[edition: Pro]

Bends the pitch of **Sound Class** and its child classes by **Pitch Change** and back, with the same attack, hold and release settings as Sound Class Duck. -0.3 plays 30% lower and 0.5 plays 50% higher. When several tracks change the same class, the pitch farthest from normal wins.

- **Class:** `UFeelStep_PitchBend`, module FeelCore.
- **Default channel:** `Feel.Audio.Mix`.
- **Comfort group:** none, only Master applies.
- **Editor preview:** yes.
- **Track length:** needs a length.
- **New tracks start with:** a flat intensity curve at 1.

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Sound Class** | None | Sound class to adjust, including its child classes. Leave empty for the project's default sound class (Project Settings > Audio). |
| **Attack Fraction** | 0.1 | Portion of the track spent moving to the full adjustment. Range 0 to 1. |
| **Release Fraction** | 0.4 | Portion of the track spent returning to normal. Range 0 to 1. |
| **Pitch Change** | -0.3 | Pitch change at full strength: -0.3 plays 30% lower, 0.5 plays 50% higher. Range -0.9 to 2. |

### Low-pass Sweep {#step_low_pass_sweep}

[edition: Pro]

Filters the high frequencies of **Sound Class** and its child classes down to **Cutoff Frequency** at full strength, then opens the filter again, with the same attack, hold and release settings as Sound Class Duck. The cutoff moves between fixed levels rather than continuously: no filter (20000 Hz), 8000, 4000, 2000, 1000, 500 and 250 Hz. The level closest to the current cutoff is used. When several tracks change the same class, the lowest cutoff wins.

- **Class:** `UFeelStep_LowPassSweep`, module FeelCore.
- **Default channel:** `Feel.Audio.Mix`.
- **Comfort group:** none, only Master applies.
- **Editor preview:** yes.
- **Track length:** needs a length.
- **New tracks start with:** a flat intensity curve at 1.

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Sound Class** | None | Sound class to adjust, including its child classes. Leave empty for the project's default sound class (Project Settings > Audio). |
| **Attack Fraction** | 0.1 | Portion of the track spent moving to the full adjustment. Range 0 to 1. |
| **Release Fraction** | 0.4 | Portion of the track spent returning to normal. Range 0 to 1. |
| **Cutoff Frequency** | 800 Hz | Cutoff frequency at full strength. Lower is more muffled. Range 100 to 20000. |

## Haptics steps {#ref_steps_haptics}

Haptics steps vibrate the controller of the target's local player. On Windows, Xbox controllers vibrate directly; PlayStation and other controllers vibrate when the game runs through Steam with Steam Input.

### Force Feedback Curve {#step_force_feedback_curve}

[edition: Lite and Pro]

Vibrates the controller with four motor strengths, which are the values at full intensity. The motion shape (Kick by default) and the intensity curve shape the vibration over the track. **Ripple Frequency** adds regular dips in strength, for textures such as an engine or a heartbeat, and **Ripple Depth** sets how deep the dips go. When several plays vibrate the same controller, the strongest value wins for each motor.

- **Class:** `UFeelStep_ForceFeedbackCurve`, module FeelCore.
- **Default channel:** `Feel.Haptics`.
- **Comfort group:** Haptics.
- **Editor preview:** no, the track shows **No preview**.
- **Track length:** needs a length.
- **New tracks start with:** a flat intensity curve at 1.
- **Motion shape:** Kick by default; the shape settings are described in [ref: ref_motion_settings].

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Left Large** | 1 | Left heavy motor strength at full intensity. Range 0 to 1. |
| **Left Small** | 0.4 | Left light motor strength at full intensity. Range 0 to 1. |
| **Right Large** | 1 | Right heavy motor strength at full intensity. Range 0 to 1. |
| **Right Small** | 0.4 | Right light motor strength at full intensity. Range 0 to 1. |
| **Ripple Frequency** | 0 Hz | Adds texture: the strength ripples this many times per second, like an engine or a heartbeat. 0 is a steady rumble. Range 0 to 60. |
| **Ripple Depth** | 0.5 | How deep the ripple dips, from 0 (no dip) to 1 (fully off at each dip). Range 0 to 1. Editable only when **Ripple Frequency** is above 0. |

Checks when the recipe is saved:

- Warning: "Force Feedback Curve has every motor at 0, so it never vibrates."

### Haptic Pattern {#step_haptic_pattern}

[edition: Pro]

Plays a Force Feedback Effect asset on the controller when the track starts, with the asset's own curves. With **Looping** on and a track length, the effect repeats until the track ends. **Stop with Track** stops it when the track ends or the recipe stops. The effect ignores time dilation, so hitstops do not stretch it. The track's intensity does not change the effect's strength. A player's Haptics comfort still applies: at 0 the track does not play, and with **Apply Comfort to Engine Force Feedback** on, the player controller's force feedback scale reduces this effect like any other vibration.

- **Class:** `UFeelStep_HapticPattern`, module FeelCore.
- **Default channel:** `Feel.Haptics`.
- **Comfort group:** Haptics; comfort can switch the effect off (Haptics at 0) but cannot make it weaker.
- **Editor preview:** no, the track shows **No preview**.
- **Track length:** can be an instant track (length 0).
- **New tracks start with:** an intensity curve that fades from 1 to 0.

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Effect** | None | Force feedback effect to play. |
| **Looping** | Off | Repeat the effect until the track ends. Only for tracks with a length. |
| **Stop with Track** | On | Stop the effect when the track ends or the recipe stops, even if it is not looping. |

Checks when the recipe is saved:

- Error: "Haptic Pattern has no force feedback effect."

## UI steps {#ref_steps_ui}

Widget Punch, Widget Shake and Widget Flash need a widget target ([see: node_target_from_widget]); on other targets they do nothing. They change the widget's render transform and color, which leaves the layout alone, and FeelKit restores both afterwards. Number Pop draws text over the game view of the target's player and works with any target.

### Widget Punch {#step_widget_punch}

[edition: Pro]

Scales, moves and turns the widget target by **Scale Change**, **Translation** and **Angle Degrees** at the peak and back; the default Spring shape overshoots before it settles. Offsets from several tracks add up.

- **Class:** `UFeelStep_WidgetPunch`, module FeelCore.
- **Default channel:** `Feel.UI`.
- **Comfort group:** none, only Master applies.
- **Editor preview:** no, the track shows **No preview**.
- **Track length:** needs a length.
- **New tracks start with:** a flat intensity curve at 1.
- **Motion shape:** Spring by default; the shape settings are described in [ref: ref_motion_settings].

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Scale Change** | (0.2, 0.2) | Scale change at the peak: 0.2 makes the widget 20% larger. |
| **Translation** | (0, 0) slate units | Movement at the peak, in slate units. |
| **Angle Degrees** | 0° | Rotation at the peak. |

### Widget Shake {#step_widget_shake}

[edition: Pro]

Shakes the widget target with smooth noise on each axis. **Amplitude** is the largest movement at the start, **Frequency** the speed, and **Decay** how quickly the shake dies over the track: 0 keeps full strength and 1 fades linearly. **Angle Amplitude** adds rotation.

- **Class:** `UFeelStep_WidgetShake`, module FeelCore.
- **Default channel:** `Feel.UI`.
- **Comfort group:** none, only Master applies.
- **Editor preview:** no, the track shows **No preview**.
- **Track length:** needs a length.
- **New tracks start with:** a flat intensity curve at 1.

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Amplitude** | (8, 3) slate units | Largest movement at the start, in slate units. |
| **Angle Amplitude** | 0° | Largest rotation at the start. |
| **Frequency** | 30 Hz | Shake speed. Range 1 to 80. |
| **Decay** | 1 | How quickly the shake dies down: 0 keeps full strength, 1 fades linearly, higher fades faster. Range 0 to 8. |

### Widget Flash {#step_widget_flash}

[edition: Pro]

Tints the widget target toward **Color** and back. It applies to user widgets, images and text blocks (their color and opacity) and to borders (their brush color). **Strength** sets how far the color moves at the peak. When several tracks tint the same widget, the strongest wins.

- **Class:** `UFeelStep_WidgetFlash`, module FeelCore.
- **Default channel:** `Feel.UI`.
- **Comfort group:** none, only Master applies.
- **Editor preview:** no, the track shows **No preview**.
- **Track length:** needs a length.
- **New tracks start with:** a flat intensity curve at 1.
- **Motion shape:** Kick by default; the shape settings are described in [ref: ref_motion_settings].

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Color** | R 1, G 0.2, B 0.2 | Color at the peak. |
| **Strength** | 1 | How far the widget color moves toward Color at the peak. Range 0 to 1. |

### Number Pop {#step_number_pop}

[edition: Pro]

Shows a number or short text that pops up at the target, or at the play's Location, and floats up over the game view of the target's player. With **Value Parameter** set, it shows that recipe parameter's value with **Decimals** digits after the point; otherwise it shows **Text**. **Prefix** and **Suffix** are added around it. The text appears at **Pop Scale** times its size and settles, rises by **Rise Distance** and gets a random sideways offset of up to **Spread**, so repeated pops do not cover each other. It stays for the length of the track, or for **Default Lifetime** on an instant track. With **Scale with Intensity** on, the font size follows the intensity, between 0.25 and 4 times **Font Size**.

- **Class:** `UFeelStep_NumberPop`, module FeelCore.
- **Default channel:** `Feel.UI`.
- **Comfort group:** none, only Master applies.
- **Editor preview:** no, the track shows **No preview**.
- **Track length:** can be an instant track (length 0).
- **New tracks start with:** an intensity curve that fades from 1 to 0.

|---|---|---|
| >> Text |  |  |
| **Value Parameter** | None | Parameter whose value is shown. Leave empty to show Text instead. |
| **Decimals** | 0 | Digits after the decimal point when showing a parameter value. Range 0 to 4. |
| **Text** | empty | Text shown when no value parameter is set. |
| **Prefix** | empty | Added before the text. |
| **Suffix** | empty | Added after the text. |
| >> Style |  |  |
| **Color** | White (R 1, G 1, B 1) | Text color. |
| **Font Size** | 28 | Font size at intensity 1. Range 6 to 200. |
| **Scale with Intensity** | On | Grow the text with the track's intensity. |
| >> Placement |  |  |

| **World Offset** | (0, 0, 60) cm | World offset from that location, in centimeters. |
| >> Motion |  |  |
| **Rise Distance** | 60 slate units | How far the text floats up on screen over its lifetime, in slate units. At least 0. |
| **Spread** | 24 slate units | Random sideways spread, in slate units, so repeated pops do not stack. At least 0. |
| **Pop Scale** | 1.6 | Size at the moment the text appears, relative to its settled size. Range 0.1 to 4. |

## Spawn steps {#ref_steps_spawn}

Spawn steps create something in the world when the track starts and leave it to the engine afterwards.

### Spawn Decal {#step_spawn_decal}

[edition: Pro]

Spawns **Decal Material** at the play's Location, or at the target when the play passed none; with **Location** set to Target it always uses the target. With **Find Surface** on, FeelKit looks for a surface from that point along the projection direction, which is down unless the play passed a Normal, up to **Surface Search Distance** beyond the edge of the target, and places the decal on it, facing the surface. **Random Rotation** turns each decal around the normal. The decal stays for **Lifetime** and then fades over **Fade Out Time**. The decal material must use the Deferred Decal domain; `M_FK_Decal_Scorch` in /FeelKit/Samples/Materials is a sample.

- **Class:** `UFeelStep_SpawnDecal`, module FeelCore.
- **Default channel:** `Feel.Spawn`.
- **Comfort group:** none, only Master applies.
- **Editor preview:** yes.
- **Track length:** can be an instant track (length 0).
- **New tracks start with:** an intensity curve that fades from 1 to 0.

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Decal Material** | None | Decal material (Deferred Decal material domain). |
| **Decal Size** | (16, 48, 48) cm | Decal size: X is projection depth, Y and Z the width and height. |
| **Location** | Play Location or Target | Where the decal appears. |
| **Lifetime** | 5 s | Seconds before the decal starts fading. At least 0. |
| **Fade Out Time** | 1 s | Fade-out length. At least 0. |
| **Random Rotation** | On | Rotate the decal randomly around the normal for variety. |
| **Find Surface** | On | Looks for a surface from the spawn point along the direction the decal projects (down, unless the play gives a Normal), and places the decal on it with that surface's orientation. Useful because actor locations are usually above the ground: a character's location is the middle of its capsule. Off places the decal exactly at the spawn point. |
| **Surface Search Distance** | 500 cm | How far to look for a surface, beyond the edge of the target (for a character: below its feet). At least 0. Editable only when **Find Surface** is on. |

Checks when the recipe is saved:

- Error: "Spawn Decal has no decal material."

### Spawn Particle {#step_spawn_particle}

[edition: Pro]

Spawns the Niagara system **System** at the play's Location or at the target, or attached to the target at **Attach Socket Name** when **Attach To Target** is on. **Orient to Normal** turns the system's up axis to the play's Normal. **Parameters** pass values into float user parameters of the system when it spawns: the value of a recipe parameter, or the track's intensity when **Recipe Parameter** is empty. With **Deactivate with Track** on and a track length, the system stops spawning new particles when the track ends or the recipe stops. The step is in the FeelNiagara module, which is enabled with FeelKit.

- **Class:** `UFeelStep_SpawnParticle`, module FeelNiagara.
- **Default channel:** `Feel.Spawn`.
- **Comfort group:** none, only Master applies.
- **Editor preview:** yes.
- **Track length:** can be an instant track (length 0).
- **New tracks start with:** an intensity curve that fades from 1 to 0.

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **System** | None | Particle system to spawn. |
| **Location** | Play Location or Target | Where the system appears when not attached. |
| **Attach to Target** | Off | Follow the target component instead of staying where it spawned. |
| **Attach Socket Name** | None | Socket or bone to attach to. Editable only when **Attach to Target** is on. |
| **Orient to Normal** | On | Point the system's up axis along the play context's Normal when the play passed one. |
| **Scale** | (1, 1, 1) | Scale of the spawned system. |
| **Parameters** | empty | Values passed into user parameters of the system. |
| **Deactivate with Track** | On | Stop the system spawning new particles when the track ends or the recipe stops. Only for tracks with a length. |

Each entry of **Parameters**:

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Field | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **User Parameter** | None | Float user parameter of the system, without the "User." prefix. |
| **Recipe Parameter** | None | Recipe parameter whose value is passed. Leave empty to pass the track's intensity. |

Checks when the recipe is saved:

- Error: "Spawn Particle has no particle system."

## Meta steps {#ref_steps_meta}

Meta steps play other steps and recipes, or call into game code.

### Play Recipe {#step_play_recipe}

[edition: Pro]

Plays another recipe inside this track. The inner recipe starts with the track and plays for as long as the track lasts, so give the track at least the inner recipe's length. It uses the same target, context and parameters, and **Intensity Scale** multiplies its intensity on top of this track's intensity. Its tracks keep their own channels and comfort settings. Recipes nest up to a depth of 4; deeper tracks are skipped, which also stops a recipe from playing itself without end.

- **Class:** `UFeelStep_Recipe`, module FeelCore.
- **Default channel:** `Feel.Meta.Recipe`.
- **Comfort group:** none for the track itself; the inner recipe's tracks keep their own channels and comfort groups.
- **Editor preview:** yes, exactly like the inner recipe.
- **Track length:** needs a length.
- **New tracks start with:** a flat intensity curve at 1.

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Recipe** | None | Recipe to play inside this track. |
| **Intensity Scale** | 1 | Multiplies the inner recipe's intensity, on top of this track's intensity curve. At least 0. |

Checks when the recipe is saved:

- Error: "Play Recipe has no recipe."
- Error: "Play Recipe plays the recipe it is in."

### Random Choice {#step_random_choice}

[edition: Pro]

Plays one of its **Options**, picked at random for each play by **Weight**: an option with weight 2 is picked twice as often as one with weight 1. The pick is fixed for the whole play, so scrubbing shows the same option, and every new play picks again. Options without a step or with weight 0 are never picked. Checks on save include the settings of every option's step.

- **Class:** `UFeelStep_RandomChoice`, module FeelCore.
- **Default channel:** the default channel of the first option's step, or `Feel.Meta.Recipe` when there is none.
- **Comfort group:** the group of the track's channel.
- **Editor preview:** as the step of the option picked for the preview play.
- **Track length:** needs a length.
- **New tracks start with:** an intensity curve that fades from 1 to 0.

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Options** | empty | Steps to choose from. |

Each entry of **Options**:

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Field | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Step** | None | Step played when this option is chosen. |
| **Weight** | 1 | Relative chance of this option. An option with weight 2 is picked twice as often as one with weight 1. At least 0. |

Checks when the recipe is saved:

- Warning: "Random Choice has no option with a step and a weight above 0, so it plays nothing."

### Blueprint Event {#step_blueprint_event}

[edition: Lite and Pro]

Calls a custom event or function by name when the track starts (**Start Event Name**) and when it ends (**Stop Event Name**). **Receiver** chooses the object that is called: the target actor, the pawn or the player controller of the target's local player, or the Level Blueprint. The event must take no inputs, or a single float that receives the track's intensity; with any other inputs, or when the name is not found, nothing is called and a warning appears in the log under LogFeelSteps. With **Call Stop Event when Interrupted** on, the stop event is also called when the recipe is stopped early. Blueprint calls need a game world, so the editor preview does not make them.

- **Class:** `UFeelStep_BlueprintEvent`, module FeelCore.
- **Default channel:** `Feel.Meta.Event`.
- **Comfort group:** none, only Master applies.
- **Editor preview:** no, the track shows **No preview**.
- **Track length:** can be an instant track (length 0).
- **New tracks start with:** an intensity curve that fades from 1 to 0.

{widths: 26,20,54}
| Property | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Receiver** | Target Actor | Object that receives the calls. |
| **Start Event Name** | None | Custom event or function called when the track starts. Leave empty to skip. |
| **Stop Event Name** | None | Custom event or function called when the track ends. Leave empty to skip. |
| **Call Stop Event when Interrupted** | On | Also call the stop event when the recipe is stopped early. |

Checks when the recipe is saved:

- Warning: "Blueprint Event has no start or stop event name, so it does nothing."
